description: The extended FOCUS ACCU: each spectral band SUSTAINS until louder data appears in that band (per-channel max-hold accumulator), with per-second decay and glissando of the held material - and, unlike focus accu (static duration), the accumulator RINGS PAST THE END of the input, appending a resonant tail until the held spectrum decays to (float-)zero. DEFAULT DIVERGENCE (first-class, source-verified): the banner claims decay 'Default 1.0 (no attenuation)', but superaccu.c sets default_val[SUPACDECAY] = 0.01 - and the enforced range is 0.00001-0.9, so 'no attenuation' is not even legal; flag-less runs equal -d0.01 (verified: identical durations). Tail model (calibrated on ~0.8-peak sources): tail ~= 14.5/-ln(decay) seconds - measured outputs 2.023 s -> 4.83 (default), 7.68 (-d0.1), 12.89 (-d0.3), 20.97 (-d0.5); indur-independent (3.02 s -> same tail). The tail ends at an ABSOLUTE level threshold, so it is content-dependent: flat noise rang ~20% longer than the tone at the same decay (6.90 s vs 5.66 s at -d0.1) - the duration expression is a staging estimate, not sample-exact. decay and glis both accept breakpoint files (verified live); mode 2 forces resonance starts to the tempered scale, modes 3/4 to a tuning file. Deterministic.
musical_use: Turns any evolving sound into its own reverberant resonator: every band holds its loudest recent value, so the spectrum only ever accretes until decay lets it fall - speech becomes a swelling organ of its own vowels (the manual quotes a 6 s speech file ringing for 78 s at decay 0.88... on this build decay caps at 0.9 and the tail is level-dependent). decay IS the reverb-time dial: 0.01 gives a discreet ~3 s halo, 0.3-0.5 tails of ten to twenty seconds, 0.9 minutes-long drones - budget disk space before pushing it high, and remember a decay BREAKPOINT rising late in the file can stretch the tail far beyond the scalar prediction (verified: a 0.5->0.8 ramp gave a 61.7 s output from 2 s). glis makes the held material slide (octaves/sec, negative = downward) - shimmering Risset-like drift on sustained sources; add -r to let glissing bands migrate to their proper channels (only meaningful while glissing; a no-op otherwise). Follow with stretch time for the classic slow-motion resonance wash, or spectune/tunevary to pitch the accumulated field. Mode 2 (tempered) is the celebrated one for speech; this entry pins mode 1, the free version.

decay.description: Sustained channel data attenuates by this factor per second (CDP-enforced 0.00001-0.9, refusals at 0 and 0.95 verbatim '(0.000010 to 0.900000)'). DEFAULT IS 0.01 (source), not the banner's impossible '1.0'. Directly sets the resonant-tail length (~14.5/-ln(decay) s). BREAKPOINT-CAPABLE (verified: out-of-range values inside a brkfile are range-checked 'in brkpntfile ...', and a valid 0.5->0.8 ramp ran, output 61.7 s); the envelope keeps being read through the tail, holding its last value.

glis.description: Held channel data glisses at this many octaves per second (banner 'Approx Range: -11.7 to 11.7'; source bound is MAXGLISRATE/frametime - analysis-rate-dependent, and -g12 was accepted on the probe file). Changes content, not duration (verified). Breakpoint-capable (verified: brk render differs from scalar).

reassign.description: Reassign glissing pitches to the appropriate channels once they leave their own (source: active only while glissing AND only when a better channel is quieter). Accepted; byte-identical no-op on the probe source even with -g2 - effect is source-dependent. Bool switch: execute()-side until the engine accepts bools.

examples.expected_use: Per-band sustain with the default 0.01/s decay; ~2.8 s resonant tail appended after the input ends.

examples.description: Long ringing accumulation with downward drift.
examples.expected_use: Held spectrum sinks half an octave per second while ringing ~19 s past the input - budget the file size.

known_issues: BANNER DIVERGENCE (first-class): decay's documented default '1.0 (no attenuation)' is outside the enforced range (0.00001-0.9); the real source default is 0.01 (flag-less == -d0.01, duration-verified). There is no 'no attenuation' setting.

DURATION EXTENDS past the input: outdur = indur + resonant tail, tail ~= 14.5/-ln(decay) s (probes: decay 0.01/0.1/0.3/0.5 -> tails 2.80/5.66/10.87/18.95 s on a tone; indur-independent). The tail ends at an ABSOLUTE amplitude threshold, so it is CONTENT-DEPENDENT: broadband/louder material rings longer (flat noise: 3.40/6.90 s at 0.01/0.1 - ~20% over the model). Treat the pre-flight as a +/-20% staging estimate, and expect far longer outputs when a decay breakpoint rises above its starting value (0.5->0.8 ramp -> 61.7 s from 2 s).
Contrast focus accu (curated): same sustain idea, but STATIC duration - choose superaccu when you want the ring-out, focus accu when you want the length preserved.

Siblings: mode 2 = resonance starts forced to the tempered scale (verified running, distinct output); modes 3/4 take a tuning file that - despite the banner calling it 'a set of frequencies' - is parsed as MIDI pitch values (verbatim refusal for 220: 'Pitch out of range (10.000000 - 14700.000000)... file tun1.txt'; MIDI-valued files run). Divergence recorded for their future curation.
-r verified a byte-identical no-op unless material is actually glissing into other channels - source-dependent, not a bug.
Deterministic (byte-identical data chunks 1.2 s apart). 'WARNING: failed to write PEAK data' family warning harmless.
